(1) the softmax activation hampers the detection of adversarials and out-of-distributions examples and (2) the logits are better suited for this task than the softmax probabilities.
the softmax activation is partly responsible for the overconfidence issue in neural networks and that the logits provide a better representation of the network's predictions.

the question of how the softmax activation function hinders the detection and the understanding of adversarial and Out-of-distribution examples.
the question: “Why do adversarial examples work?” We argue that this is not because neural networks are “too good” or “too powerful”, but because they are too “confident” about the data they are fed.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the softmax activation is responsible for a part of the overconfidence issue observed in neural networks, but not the whole part, as it has been shown that other components of the network also play a role.
the use of the softmax activation is not recommended in safety-critical systems.

the softmax activation should not be used as a last layer in neural networks if one is interested in the detection of out-of-distribution or adversarial examples, and if a reliable confidence estimate is required.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the overconfidence of neural networks is not only a problem of the loss function but also of the softmax function.
the softmax activation is a source of information loss for the detection of out-of-distribution or adversarial examples.
the softmax activation should be replaced by another activation function in order to improve the detection of adversarials and out-of-distributions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the logits should not be ignored, and that the softmax probabilities should not be used as a proxy for the confidence of a prediction.
a reliable confidence estimate for a given prediction can be obtained by directly using the logits instead of the softmax probabilities.
the softmax activation is a key component in the overconfidence issue, and that it should be taken into account for the design of new detectors for adversarial and out of distribution examples.
